audit_status.source_base: Greek Hebrews text tradition with extensive ancestral Scripture memory; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for trust definition, ancestors, women, suffering, better resurrection, cloud of witnesses setup.

verses.restored: Now trust is substance/assurance of things hoped for, evidence/conviction of matters not seen.

familiar.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

modern.text: Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.

original.text: Ἔστιν δὲ πίστις ἐλπιζομένων ὑπόστασις, πραγμάτων ἔλεγχος οὐ βλεπομένων·

verses.restored: For by this the elders were witnessed.

familiar.text: For by it the elders obtained a good report.

modern.text: This is why the ancients were commended.

original.text: ἐν ταύτῃ γὰρ ἐμαρτυρήθησαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι.

verses.restored: By trust we understand the ages to have been framed by word of Divine, so that what is seen has not come from things appearing.

familiar.text: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.

modern.text: By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible. The Faith of Abel, Enoch, Noah (Genesis 4—9)

original.text: πίστει νοοῦμεν κατηρτίσθαι τοὺς αἰῶνας ῥήματι θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων ⸂τὸ βλεπόμενον⸃ γεγονέναι.

verses.restored: By trust Abel offered to the Divine a better sacrifice than Cain, through which he was witnessed to be righteous/just, the Divine witnessing upon his gifts; and through it, having died, he still speaks.

familiar.text: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.

modern.text: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. By faith he was commended as righteous when God gave approval to his gifts. And by faith he still speaks, even though he is dead.

original.text: Πίστει πλείονα θυσίαν Ἅβελ παρὰ Κάϊν προσήνεγκεν τῷ θεῷ, διʼ ἧς ἐμαρτυρήθη εἶναι δίκαιος, μαρτυροῦντος ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ ⸂τοῦ θεοῦ⸃, καὶ διʼ αὐτῆς ἀποθανὼν ἔτι ⸀λαλεῖ.

verses.restored: By trust Enoch was transferred so as not to see death, and he was not found because the Divine transferred him; for before the transfer he had been witnessed to have pleased the Divine.

familiar.text: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.

modern.text: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death: “He could not be found, because God had taken him away.” For before he was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God.

original.text: Πίστει Ἑνὼχ μετετέθη τοῦ μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον, καὶ οὐχ ηὑρίσκετο διότι μετέθηκεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεός· πρὸ γὰρ τῆς ⸀μεταθέσεως μεμαρτύρηται εὐαρεστηκέναι τῷ θεῷ,

verses.restored: But apart from trust it is impossible to please, for the one drawing near to Divine must trust that he is and that he becomes rewarder of those seeking him.

familiar.text: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

modern.text: And without faith it is impossible to please God, because anyone who approaches Him must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who earnestly seek Him.

original.text: χωρὶς δὲ πίστεως ἀδύνατον εὐαρεστῆσαι, πιστεῦσαι γὰρ δεῖ τὸν προσερχόμενον τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἔστιν καὶ τοῖς ἐκζητοῦσιν αὐτὸν μισθαποδότης γίνεται.

verses.restored: By trust Noah, having been warned concerning things not yet seen, moved with reverent care, prepared ark for salvation/healing of his household, through which he condemned the world-system and became heir of righteousness/justice according to trust.

familiar.text: By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.

modern.text: By faith Noah, when warned about things not yet seen, in godly fear built an ark to save his family. By faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith. The Faith of Abraham and Sarah (Genesis 15—22; Romans 4:1–12)

original.text: πίστει χρηματισθεὶς Νῶε περὶ τῶν μηδέπω βλεπομένων εὐλαβηθεὶς κατεσκεύασεν κιβωτὸν εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ, διʼ ἧς κατέκρινεν τὸν κόσμον, καὶ τῆς κατὰ πίστιν δικαιοσύνης ἐγένετο κληρονόμος.

verses.restored: By trust Abraham obeyed when called to go out to place he was about to receive as inheritance, and he went out not knowing where he was going.

familiar.text: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.

modern.text: By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, without knowing where he was going.

original.text: ⸀Πίστει καλούμενος Ἀβραὰμ ὑπήκουσεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς ⸀τόπον ὃν ἤμελλεν λαμβάνειν εἰς κληρονομίαν, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν μὴ ἐπιστάμενος ποῦ ἔρχεται.

verses.restored: By trust he sojourned in land of promise as foreign land, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of same promise.

familiar.text: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:

modern.text: By faith he dwelt in the promised land as a stranger in a foreign country. He lived in tents, as did Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise.

original.text: πίστει παρῴκησεν εἰς γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ὡς ἀλλοτρίαν, ἐν σκηναῖς κατοικήσας μετὰ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ τῶν συγκληρονόμων τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῆς αὐτῆς·

verses.restored: For he awaited the city having foundations, whose artisan and maker is Divine.

familiar.text: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

modern.text: For he was looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God.

original.text: ἐξεδέχετο γὰρ τὴν τοὺς θεμελίους ἔχουσαν πόλιν, ἧς τεχνίτης καὶ δημιουργὸς ὁ θεός.

verses.restored: By trust Sarah herself received power for seed/offspring, even beyond season of age, since she considered trustworthy the One promising.

familiar.text: Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.

modern.text: By faith Sarah, even though she was barren and beyond the proper age, was enabled to conceive a child, because she considered Him faithful who had promised.

original.text: πίστει καὶ ⸂αὐτῇ Σάρρᾳ⸃ δύναμιν εἰς καταβολὴν σπέρματος ἔλαβεν καὶ παρὰ καιρὸν ⸀ἡλικίας, ἐπεὶ πιστὸν ἡγήσατο τὸν ἐπαγγειλάμενον·

verses.restored: Therefore also from one, and these things having been made dead, were born as stars of heaven in multitude and like innumerable sand by seashore.

familiar.text: Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.

modern.text: And so from one man, and he as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore.

original.text: διὸ καὶ ἀφʼ ἑνὸς ἐγεννήθησαν, καὶ ταῦτα νενεκρωμένου, καθὼς τὰ ἄστρα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τῷ πλήθει καὶ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος ἡ παρὰ τὸ χεῖλος τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ ἀναρίθμητος.

verses.restored: According to trust all these died, not having received the promises, but seeing them from afar and greeting them, and confessing that they were strangers and sojourners upon earth.

familiar.text: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

modern.text: All these people died in faith, without having received the things they were promised. However, they saw them and welcomed them from afar. And they acknowledged that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.

original.text: Κατὰ πίστιν ἀπέθανον οὗτοι πάντες, μὴ ⸀λαβόντες τὰς ἐπαγγελίας, ἀλλὰ πόρρωθεν αὐτὰς ἰδόντες καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι, καὶ ὁμολογήσαντες ὅτι ξένοι καὶ παρεπίδημοί εἰσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

verses.restored: For those saying such things make clear that they seek homeland.

familiar.text: For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.

modern.text: Now those who say such things show that they are seeking a country of their own.

original.text: οἱ γὰρ τοιαῦτα λέγοντες ἐμφανίζουσιν ὅτι πατρίδα ἐπιζητοῦσιν.

verses.restored: And if indeed they remembered that from which they went out, they would have had opportunity to return.

familiar.text: And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.

modern.text: If they had been thinking of the country they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.

original.text: καὶ εἰ μὲν ἐκείνης ⸀μνημονεύουσιν ἀφʼ ἧς ⸀ἐξέβησαν, εἶχον ἂν καιρὸν ἀνακάμψαι·

verses.restored: But now they desire better, that is, heavenly; therefore the Divine is not ashamed of them, to be called their Divine, for he prepared for them a city.

familiar.text: But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.

modern.text: Instead, they were longing for a better country, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them.

original.text: νῦν δὲ κρείττονος ὀρέγονται, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ἐπουρανίου. διὸ οὐκ ἐπαισχύνεται αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς θεὸς ἐπικαλεῖσθαι αὐτῶν, ἡτοίμασεν γὰρ αὐτοῖς πόλιν.

verses.restored: By trust Abraham, being tested, offered Isaac; and the one receiving promises was offering the only/beloved,

familiar.text: By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son,

modern.text: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar. He who had received the promises was ready to offer his one and only son,

original.text: Πίστει προσενήνοχεν Ἀβραὰμ τὸν Ἰσαὰκ πειραζόμενος, καὶ τὸν μονογενῆ προσέφερεν ὁ τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἀναδεξάμενος,

verses.restored: to whom it was spoken: In Isaac your seed will be called.

familiar.text: Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:

modern.text: even though God had said to him, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”

original.text: πρὸς ὃν ἐλαλήθη ὅτι Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα,

verses.restored: reckoning that Divine was able even from dead ones to raise, from which also, in parable, he received him back.

familiar.text: Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.

modern.text: Abraham reasoned that God could raise the dead, and in a sense, he did receive Isaac back from death. The Faith of Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph (Genesis 27—50)

original.text: λογισάμενος ὅτι καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγείρειν δυνατὸς ὁ θεός· ὅθεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν παραβολῇ ἐκομίσατο.

verses.restored: By trust Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things coming.

familiar.text: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.

modern.text: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the future.

original.text: Πίστει ⸀καὶ περὶ μελλόντων εὐλόγησεν Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακὼβ καὶ τὸν Ἠσαῦ.

verses.restored: By trust Jacob, dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and worshiped upon top of his staff.

familiar.text: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.

modern.text: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff.

original.text: πίστει Ἰακὼβ ἀποθνῄσκων ἕκαστον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰωσὴφ εὐλόγησεν, καὶ προσεκύνησεν ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον τῆς ῥάβδου αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: By trust Joseph, ending life, remembered concerning the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave command concerning his bones.

familiar.text: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.

modern.text: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, spoke about the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones. The Faith of Moses (Exodus 2—15; Acts 7:20–22)

original.text: πίστει Ἰωσὴφ τελευτῶν περὶ τῆς ἐξόδου τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐμνημόνευσεν, καὶ περὶ τῶν ὀστέων αὐτοῦ ἐνετείλατο.

verses.restored: By trust Moses, having been born, was hidden three months by his parents, because they saw the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the decree of the king.

familiar.text: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.

modern.text: By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after his birth, because they saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were unafraid of the king’s edict.

original.text: Πίστει Μωϋσῆς γεννηθεὶς ἐκρύβη τρίμηνον ὑπὸ τῶν πατέρων αὐτοῦ, διότι εἶδον ἀστεῖον τὸ παιδίον καὶ οὐκ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸ διάταγμα τοῦ βασιλέως.

verses.restored: By trust Moses, having become great, refused to be called son of Pharaoh's daughter,

familiar.text: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;

modern.text: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.

original.text: πίστει Μωϋσῆς μέγας γενόμενος ἠρνήσατο λέγεσθαι υἱὸς θυγατρὸς Φαραώ,

verses.restored: choosing rather to suffer hardship with the people of the Divine than to have temporary enjoyment of sin/misalignment,

familiar.text: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;

modern.text: He chose to suffer oppression with God’s people rather than to experience the fleeting enjoyment of sin.

original.text: μᾶλλον ἑλόμενος συγκακουχεῖσθαι τῷ λαῷ τοῦ θεοῦ ἢ πρόσκαιρον ἔχειν ἁμαρτίας ἀπόλαυσιν,

verses.restored: considering reproach of Messiah greater wealth than treasures of Egypt, for he was looking away to the reward.

familiar.text: Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.

modern.text: He valued disgrace for Christ above the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to his reward.

original.text: μείζονα πλοῦτον ἡγησάμενος τῶν Αἰγύπτου θησαυρῶν τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀπέβλεπεν γὰρ εἰς τὴν μισθαποδοσίαν.

verses.restored: By trust he left Egypt, not fearing anger of the king, for he endured as seeing the unseen One.

familiar.text: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.

modern.text: By faith Moses left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger; he persevered because he saw Him who is invisible.

original.text: πίστει κατέλιπεν Αἴγυπτον, μὴ φοβηθεὶς τὸν θυμὸν τοῦ βασιλέως, τὸν γὰρ ἀόρατον ὡς ὁρῶν ἐκαρτέρησεν.

verses.restored: By trust he has kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of firstborn might not touch them.

familiar.text: Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.

modern.text: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch Israel’s own firstborn.

original.text: πίστει πεποίηκεν τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὴν πρόσχυσιν τοῦ αἵματος, ἵνα μὴ ὁ ὀλοθρεύων τὰ πρωτότοκα θίγῃ αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: By trust they passed through Red Sea as through dry land, which the Egyptians, attempting, were swallowed.

familiar.text: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.

modern.text: By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to follow, they were drowned. The Faith of Many (Joshua–Malachi)

original.text: Πίστει διέβησαν τὴν Ἐρυθρὰν Θάλασσαν ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς ⸀γῆς, ἧς πεῖραν λαβόντες οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι κατεπόθησαν.

verses.restored: By trust walls of Jericho fell, having been encircled for seven days.

familiar.text: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.

modern.text: By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had marched around them for seven days.

original.text: πίστει τὰ τείχη Ἰεριχὼ ⸀ἔπεσαν κυκλωθέντα ἐπὶ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας.

verses.restored: By trust Rahab the sex worker did not perish with those disobeying, having received the scouts with peace.

familiar.text: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.

modern.text: By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies in peace, did not perish with those who were disobedient.

original.text: πίστει Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐ συναπώλετο τοῖς ἀπειθήσασιν, δεξαμένη τοὺς κατασκόπους μετʼ εἰρήνης.

verses.restored: And what more shall I say? For time will fail me telling of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David and Samuel and the prophets,

familiar.text: And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:

modern.text: And what more shall I say? Time will not allow me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets,

original.text: Καὶ τί ἔτι λέγω; ἐπιλείψει ⸂με γὰρ⸃ διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος περὶ Γεδεών, Βαράκ, ⸀Σαμψών, Ἰεφθάε, Δαυίδ τε καὶ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν προφητῶν,

verses.restored: who through trust conquered kingdoms, worked righteousness/justice, obtained promises, shut mouths of lions,

familiar.text: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

modern.text: who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, and gained what was promised; who shut the mouths of lions,

original.text: οἳ διὰ πίστεως κατηγωνίσαντο βασιλείας, εἰργάσαντο δικαιοσύνην, ἐπέτυχον ἐπαγγελιῶν, ἔφραξαν στόματα λεόντων,

verses.restored: quenched power of fire, escaped mouths of sword, were empowered from weakness, became strong in war, turned back camps of foreigners.

familiar.text: Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.

modern.text: quenched the raging fire, and escaped the edge of the sword; who gained strength from weakness, became mighty in battle, and put foreign armies to flight.

original.text: ἔσβεσαν δύναμιν πυρός, ἔφυγον στόματα ⸀μαχαίρης, ⸀ἐδυναμώθησαν ἀπὸ ἀσθενείας, ἐγενήθησαν ἰσχυροὶ ἐν πολέμῳ, παρεμβολὰς ἔκλιναν ἀλλοτρίων·

verses.restored: Women received their dead by resurrection; others were tortured, not accepting release, so that they might obtain better resurrection.

familiar.text: Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:

modern.text: Women received back their dead, raised to life again. Others were tortured and refused their release, so that they might gain a better resurrection.

original.text: ἔλαβον γυναῖκες ἐξ ἀναστάσεως τοὺς νεκροὺς αὐτῶν· ἄλλοι δὲ ἐτυμπανίσθησαν, οὐ προσδεξάμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν, ἵνα κρείττονος ἀναστάσεως τύχωσιν·

verses.restored: Others received trial of mockings and whippings, and further, chains and imprisonment.

familiar.text: And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:

modern.text: Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.

original.text: ἕτεροι δὲ ἐμπαιγμῶν καὶ μαστίγων πεῖραν ἔλαβον, ἔτι δὲ δεσμῶν καὶ φυλακῆς·

verses.restored: They were stoned, sawn in two, tested, killed by sword; they wandered in sheepskins, goatskins, lacking, pressured, mistreated,

familiar.text: They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented;

modern.text: They were stoned, they were sawed in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went around in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed, and mistreated.

original.text: ἐλιθάσθησαν, ⸀ἐπρίσθησαν, ἐν φόνῳ ⸀μαχαίρης ἀπέθανον, περιῆλθον ἐν μηλωταῖς, ἐν αἰγείοις δέρμασιν, ὑστερούμενοι, θλιβόμενοι, κακουχούμενοι,

verses.restored: of whom the world-system was not worthy, wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and holes of the earth.

familiar.text: (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.

modern.text: The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and hid in caves and holes in the ground.

original.text: ὧν οὐκ ἦν ἄξιος ὁ κόσμος ⸀ἐπὶ ἐρημίαις πλανώμενοι καὶ ὄρεσι καὶ σπηλαίοις καὶ ταῖς ὀπαῖς τῆς γῆς·

verses.restored: And all these, having been witnessed through trust, did not receive the promise,

familiar.text: And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:

modern.text: These were all commended for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised.

original.text: ⸀καὶ πάντες μαρτυρηθέντες διὰ τῆς πίστεως οὐκ ἐκομίσαντο τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν,

verses.restored: the Divine having foreseen something better concerning us, so that apart from us they might not be completed.

familiar.text: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.

modern.text: God had planned something better for us, so that together with us they would be made perfect.

original.text: τοῦ θεοῦ περὶ ἡμῶν κρεῖττόν τι προβλεψαμένου, ἵνα μὴ χωρὶς ἡμῶν τελειωθῶσιν.

translation_notes: Trust is pistis: assurance/faithfulness/trust embodied across ancestors.
Women are active bearers of trust: Sarah, Moses' parents, Rahab, women receiving their dead.
The chapter honors Israel's ancestors; do not appropriate them in ways that erase Jewish identity.
safety_note: The suffering list honors endurance but should not romanticize persecution or imply people must remain in abuse. Hebrews 11 is witness, not coercion.
